newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares buffeted by political rollercoaster.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares buffeted by political rollercoaster.

text.p: Renewed political uncertainty in Turkey buffeted shares further on Friday in the latest twist of a rollercoaster ride which has driven the nervous market down 10.5 percent this week, brokers said.

Islamist-led coalition plans to seek parliamentary debate of National Security Council (NSC) efforts to quell religious activism sparked a four percent morning sell-off, following on the heels of an eight percent leap on Thursday.

The IMKB National-100 index later recovered to end the day down 2.63 percent, or 39 points, at 1,443. Trading volume dived to 19.91 trillion lira ($160 million) from an unusually high 38.96 trillion a day earlier as investors steered clear of trade dominated by political developments.

"The stock exchange's movement is tied to news coming from Ankara. Economic data is taking a backseat," said Hak Securities deputy manager Yalcin Arican, adding that the market will continue to mirror uncertainty in the political arena.

Dealers said a decline in the index to an intraday low of 1,418 was also driven by a media report that a close aide to Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan had called for early elections to clear up the row with the military.
The concerns were calmed by Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller who ruled out early elections: "There will be no such thing. The government will continue," she told reporters.
"It was a good fillip...The decision to keep the government going had a relatively positive impact," said Pay Securities broker Hakan Catana.
Turkish bond yields eased slightly to around 100 percent from 101-102 percent on Thursday amid higher liquidity, although demand was limited by the political unease, dealers said.
The lira continued to weaken in the face of underlying dollar strength, easing to 124,400 against the dollar from 124,320 at Thursday's close.

A 15-percent stock market decline in the first three days of the week was partially erased on Thursday after Erbakan calmed political tension by signing up to an NSC statement aimed at restraining a rise in Islamist activism since he came to power.
The coalition's efforts to push ahead with major privatisations had been rewarded by a 65 percent gain on the stock market this year by last Friday's close.
But inflation data showing annual price rises of just under 80 percent in February showed that more progress on the economy was needed, brokers said.

They said the market sought further reassurance going into the weekend about the future of the alliance between Erbakan's Welfare Party and Ciller's conservatives before a resumption of the uptrend could resume.

"The market is fully indexed to politics. The index may plunge to the 1,300 level if the government falls, otherwise it will be squeezed between 1,400 and 1,450 if uncertainty continues," said dealer Koray Cervatoglu.
